title: Mallorca vs Ibiza: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Mallorca and Ibiza based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

categories.summary: Mallorca is a study in contrasts: the Serra de Tramuntana mountains tumble dramatically into the sea in the northwest, while the south and east coast offer calm turquoise bays with powder-white sand. categories.summary: Ibiza runs roughly 25–40% more expensive than Mallorca for standard tourist spending. faqs.question: Is Mallorca or Ibiza better for first-time visitors?
faqs.answer: Mallorca is the better first-timer choice for most travelers. It's significantly larger (3,640 km² vs Ibiza's 572 km²), offers more variety — stunning beaches, mountains, a great capital city in Palma, and cultural depth — and costs less. faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Mallorca or Ibiza?
faqs.answer: Mallorca is significantly cheaper. A mid-range trip to Mallorca runs €80–120/day (budget accommodation €50–100/night, restaurants €12–25/main course). faqs.question: Which has better beaches, Mallorca or Ibiza?
faqs.answer: It's a genuine tie — both have some of the best beaches in the Mediterranean. Mallorca's standouts: Cala Formentor (dramatic cliff backdrop), Platja de Muro (long, calm bay), Cala de Sa Nau (intimate cove), and Cala Mondragó (protected natural park). faqs.answer: Yes, but with caveats. Ibiza's north and east (Sant Joan, Santa Gertrudis, Benirràs) are genuinely beautiful and rural — hippie markets, authentic Spanish restaurants, quiet coves. faqs.answer: Mallorca: 7–10 days to do it justice. faqs.question: Can you do a day trip from Mallorca to Ibiza?
faqs.answer: Technically yes — there are ferry connections from Palma to Ibiza Town (around 2h30m–4h depending on the service, from €40–60 each way on Baleària or Trasmediterranea). faqs.question: What is the best area to stay in Mallorca?
faqs.answer: Palma de Mallorca is the best base for most travelers — great food scene, the cathedral, nightlife, and easy access to the rest of the island via car hire. faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Mallorca vs Ibiza?
faqs.answer: Both islands peak in June–August with warm seas (26–28°C water temperature) but heavy crowds and high prices. The best time for both is May or September–early October: warm enough for swimming (23–25°C water), fewer tourists, lower prices (accommodation drops 30–40%), and the landscape is gorgeous.
